content_html:
Dust mites live mainly in mattresses, bedding, upholstery, and other textiles where humidity and skin flakes support them. They cannot be eliminated completely, but exposure can be reduced when a household has confirmed allergy or compatible symptoms.

Start with the bed and bedding

Wash sheets and pillowcases on a routine that fits the household and dry them fully. Allergen-impermeable mattress and pillow covers can reduce exposure when mite sensitivity is known.

Control humidity, not just visible dust

Dust mites thrive at higher humidity. Keeping indoor humidity moderate with ventilation, air conditioning, or dehumidification can limit growth more effectively than spraying products onto fabrics.

Vacuum without redistributing particles

A well-filtered vacuum used slowly on carpets and upholstery reduces accumulated dust. Highly sensitive people may benefit from not being in the room during intensive vacuuming or dusting.

Let symptoms and diagnosis guide the effort

Visible dust does not prove a dust-mite problem, and not every home needs aggressive measures. With persistent asthma or allergy symptoms, a healthcare professional can help confirm triggers and prioritize useful changes.
